result.title: Can System-1-Style Decision Models Replace Dedicated Rerankers in RAG? A Systems Evaluation
result.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems often use a dedicated reranker to choose which retrieved candidates reach the language model. Reranking improves relevance but adds latency, so teams look for faster alternatives. System-1style decision models make direct, structured predictions instead of generating long responses. Could one provide comparable reranking quality with less inference overhead? We first screen 21 open-weight models on 11 benchmarks, then compare a promising decision model with a dedicated reranker on identical candidate lists. The default decision-model setup fails on many long candidate sets, so scoring only the requests it completes gives a misleading ranking. Limiting candidate text length largely restores reliability and makes some configurations competitive. A frozen evaluation on new retrieval data supports the reliability and ranking results, but confirms the latency requirement for only one of the two selected configurations. Across workloads, which model ranks better changes, and a tuned reranker remains faster and uses far less GPU memory. A decision model can perform competitive reranking, but replacing a reranker requires weighing quality, latency and memory together, and teams should tune the reranker they already run first.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文考察 system-1 风格的直接决策模型能否替代 RAG 中的专用 reranker：先在 11 个基准上筛选 21 个开源模型，再在相同候选列表上比较两者的排序质量、延迟与显存占用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「仅统计已完成请求会掩盖长候选集失败」以及质量-延迟-显存联合评估的做法，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 类动态计算的成本收益评测提供检查线索，但任务本身与视觉推理无直接联系，仅供核查评价方式。
